# Requirements

Rex 0.2 claims that an agent can write a web application interface with it and that an agent can operate the result. The site that explains Rex is built with Rex itself: the marketing home, the documentation, the error catalog, the API reference, the standards table and the changelog are Rex pages, rendered from the repository's own sources at build time, deployed as a static site to rex.sidioralabs.com, and gated by the same operability walk, accessibility pass and vitals gate as the demo.

## Requirement 1: The site is a Rex app

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want the site to be an ordinary Rex app on the DesignX standard so that building it tests the framework the way a user would.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. site/ is a workspace package whose pages, regions, parts, overlays and states follow the page folder convention; pnpm -C site check exits 0 with zero findings; the only dangerouslySetInnerHTML is through unsafeHtml() in the Prose part.
2. Every page renders the sidecar (script type application/rex+json, id rex-page) and the data-rex-page attribute in its prerendered HTML; the hydrated pages expose the command palette listing every page; every control carries a data-rex address and the shell navigation carries data-rex-nav.
3. The site uses the DesignX standard set from app/components/ui with a theme derived from the Rex mark, both color schemes, and no raw button, input, select, textarea, table or dialog in a region, part or overlay.

## Requirement 2: Content from the sources, never copied

**User Story:** As a reader, I want the docs, errors, API, standards and changelog on the site to be what is in the repository so that the site never drifts from the code.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every doc under docs/ and docs/recipes/ (except the README files) is a page at /docs/<slug> or /docs/recipes/<slug> whose HTML is rendered from the markdown at build time with heading ids, a table of contents and relative links rewritten to site routes; the set of pages equals the set of files.
2. Every REX code in the error catalog is a page at /errors/<code> showing code, area, message and hint, and /errors lists them grouped by area; the catalog is read from the package, not copied.
3. Every file under docs/api is a page under /api; /standards shows every [standard.*] item of spec/rex-v02/spec.kvx with its status; /changelog renders CHANGELOG.md; the version on the home page is read from packages/rex/package.json.

## Requirement 3: The home page sells Rex with true claims

**User Story:** As a developer landing on the site, I want to learn in one screen what Rex is, see proof that it works, and install it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The home page renders the hero with the mark, the tagline and subline from [design] copy, the four rules, the feature cards each linking a doc page, the install block with the version read at build time, and the footer with the repository, license and Sidiora Labs links.
2. The LiveSidecar region shows the home page's own sidecar JSON, identical in the prerendered HTML and after hydration, with the copy button addressable through data-rex.
3. Every number on the home page comes from the code at build time and a unit test asserts each against its source.

## Requirement 4: A complete static deployment

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want rex build --target static to produce a directory a static host serves completely so that the site needs no server.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rex build --target static prerenders every page (ssg and static with paths, ssr and csr as the shell document), writes rex/manifest as a JSON file, index.md next to each prerendered page, 404.html, and dist/prerender.json; the tests in packages/rex cover each output and the demo builds with the target.
2. Served by tools/serve-static.mjs, the built site makes no failed request on any page (asserted by the e2e walk with request failure tracking), the client reads the manifest inlined at build time, and a static page ships zero page JavaScript.
3. .github/workflows/site.yml builds the package and the site, runs the gates and deploys dist/client to GitHub Pages on main with site/public/CNAME set to rex.sidioralabs.com; the deployment succeeds and the deployed site answers / with data-rex-page and the sidecar.

## Requirement 5: The site passes the gates the demo passes

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want the site held to the operability, accessibility, vitals and screen-fit gates so that it is proof, not a claim.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The operability walk visits every page on phone, tablet and desktop, opens every popup trigger, reads every sidecar and invokes the addressable controls, and fails on a REX3xx region error, a page error, a console error or a failed request.
2. The no-JS walk reads every static page with JavaScript disabled and finds the content, the navigation and the sidecar; axe reports zero violations; LCP, CLS and INP are within 2500 ms, 0.1 and 200 ms; Lighthouse reports performance 95, accessibility 100, best practices 95 and SEO 95 or higher; reports are committed under site/e2e/report.
3. No page overflows horizontally on any project, every data-rex control is at least 44 px tall on phone, the navigation is a dock on phone and a sidebar on desktop, and every internal href in the built HTML resolves to a built file.

## Requirement 6: The framework learns from the site

**User Story:** As the framework author, I want every gap the site exposes fixed in packages/rex so that the next Rex app does not meet it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every gap met while building the site is an entry in spec/rex-site/qualification.kvx with the observation, and each is either fixed in packages/rex with a test or recorded as a [decision] here; task 3.3's report lists them.
2. README.md links the site and docs/releasing.md describes the site deployment; the changelog is regenerated after the work lands.
